The '''2020 FA Community Shield''' (also known as '''The FA Community Shield supported by [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 98th [[FA Community Shield]], an annual football match played between the winners of the previous season's [[2019–20 Premier League|Premier League]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], and the previous season's [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], with the latter winning on penalties after a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web |title=The FA Community Shield History |url=http://www.thefa.com/competitions/the-fa-community-shield/more/history |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=18 May 2019}}</ref> This was the fourth Charity Shield/Community Shield contested between the two clubs: Liverpool won in [[1979 FA Charity Shield|1979]] and [[1989 FA Charity Shield|1989]], while Arsenal were victorious in [[2002 FA Community Shield|2002]].<ref>{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |title=England — List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |website=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |date=5 August 2019 |access-date=27 August 2020}}</ref>

The match was televised live on [[BT Sport]] 1, [[BT Sport Extra]] 1 and [[BT Sport Ultimate]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2020/08/27/arsenal-vs-liverpool-community-shield-2020-time-kick-off-saturday/ |title=Arsenal vs Liverpool, Community Shield 2020: What time is kick-off on Saturday, what TV channel is it on and what is our prediction? |publisher=The Telegraph |date=27 August 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020}}</ref> with highlights shown later on ''[[Match of the Day]]'' on [[BBC One]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000m7x3 |title=Community Shield Highlights |publisher=BBC |access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref> Radio commentary was provided by [[Sam Matterface]] and [[Trevor Sinclair]] on [[Talksport]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Marc |last=Williams |url=https://talksport.com/football/750759/liverpool-v-arsenal-live-stream-how-to-watch-community-shield-final-for-free-kick-off-time-tv-channel-radio-coverage/ |title=Arsenal v Liverpool live stream: How to watch Community Shield final for free – kick-off time, TV channel and radio coverage |publisher=Talksport |date=26 August 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020}}</ref> The game was played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] on 29 August 2020 at [[Wembley Stadium]] and followed the [[2020 Women's FA Community Shield|Women's Community Shield]] match at the same venue, thus forming the first Community Shield double-header.<ref>{{cite web |title=ARSENAL OR CHELSEA TO PLAY PREMIER LEAGUE CHAMPIONS IN FA COMMUNITY SHIELD AT WEMBLEY |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2020/jul/29/fa-community-shield-date-confirmed-290720 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=30 July 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53751107 |title=BBC to broadcast Women's Community Shield double-header at Wembley |work=BBC Sport |date=12 August 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020}}</ref>

[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] were the holders as winners of the [[2019 FA Community Shield|2019 edition]], but did not qualify for this match, as they finished second in the [[2019–20 Premier League|Premier League]] and were knocked out of the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]] in the semi-finals.

==Background==
{{Main|2019–20 Liverpool F.C. season|2019–20 Arsenal F.C. season}}Arsenal won their 14th FA Cup title after beating Chelsea 2–1 in the [[2020 FA Cup final|final]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=McNulty|first=Phil|date=1 August 2020|title=Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea - Aubameyang double secures victory|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53546100|access-date=1 August 2020}}</ref>

Liverpool won their first [[List of English football champions|Premier League title]] since the league's formation in [[1992–93 Football League|1992]], after [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester City F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] lost 1–2 to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on 25 June 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bevan|first=Chris|date=25 June 2020|title=Liverpool win title as Chelsea beat Man City|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51884262|access-date=25 June 2020}}</ref>

== Match ==
===Summary===
In the 12th minute, [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] put Arsenal into the lead, receiving the ball on the left he cut in and curled a left-footed shot from just inside the penalty area into the right corner of the net past the diving [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]]. [[Takumi Minamino]] made it 1–1 in the 73rd minute with a side-footed finish to the right from six yards out after the ball broke to him in the penalty area off [[Cédric Soares]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12059158/arsenal-1-1-liverpool-5-4-on-pens-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-secures-community-shield-shootout-win|title=Arsenal 1-1 Liverpool (5-4 on pens): Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang secures Community Shield shootout win|date=29 August 2020|work=Sky Sports|access-date= 10 August 2021}}</ref>
The game went to a penalty shoot-out with Liverpool's [[Rhian Brewster]] the only player to miss his penalty when he struck the bar. Aubameyang scored the decisive final penalty for Arsenal, shooting to the right corner to win the match 5–4 on penalties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/aug/29/arsenal-liverpool-fa-community-shield-match-report|title=Aubameyang keeps his cool as Arsenal win Community Shield on penalties|date=29 August 2020|work=Guardian|accessdate= 10 August 2021}}</ref>
